newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Preussen Elektra, Statkraft back Sydkraft.
newsitem.headline: Preussen Elektra, Statkraft back Sydkraft.

text.p: Germany power company Preussen Elektra, the biggest private owner of Swedish power group Sydkraft AB, said on Wednesday it would stand by any decision of Sydkraft about the Barseback nuclear reactors.
"We have made it clear that all decisions for our part on this question will be made by Sydkraft's management," Preussen Elektra's head lawyer Dr Johannes Teyssen told Reuters.
"The management must also refer to the board where we have our representatives."
Preussen Elektra said it had made its position clear to Sweden's Industry and Commerce Department which on Tuesday released details of a new energy agreement.

Under the agreement, put together by the ruling Social Democrats and two other political parties, the government will close down one nuclear reactor at Barseback on Sweden's southern tip by July 1, 1998 and the second by July 1, 2001.
Barseback is fully owned by Sydkraft, the largest independent power supplier in Sweden.
Preussen Elektra holds 27.3 percent of votes and 17.6 percent of capital, according to Dagens Nyheter's owner service.
"We have been in contact with the department in Sweden and and also earlier made it clear that we respect political decisions that are made in Sweden," Teyssen said.
He said Sydkraft, and Preussen Elektra, expected full compensation for the closure of the reactors.
Sydkraft has said it wants electricity as compensation to continue to meet supplies to its customers.

Norwegian power company Statkraft, that holds 22.2 percent of votes in Sydkraft and 14.6 percent of capital, has also said it will stand by any decision made by Sydkraft. Sydkraft's board is due to meet on Friday to discuss the issue.
"We assume that Sydkraft's management will see that we get the right type of compensation in the form of new power production for Barseback's closure," Statkraft spokesman Sjur Rossholt told Reuters.
"We are not on the board yet but we expect to be sometime in April or May."
